title: Krishna Offers Sudarsana to Slay Karna
story:
The two champions were alike in the way of two mountains: both white-steeded, both at the height of their power, and now they came together in the duel the whole war had been building toward. Arjuna and Karna met like two infuriated elephants of full-grown tusks fighting for a she-elephant in her season, and the field trembled.

Like a mass of clouds meeting another mass, or a mountain meeting a mountain, they poured showers of arrows at each other — their bows twanging, their bow-strings and palms ringing, the wheels of their cars clattering — while the armies of both sides watched in silence. Karna struck first, piercing Arjuna with ten mighty shafts; Arjuna answered with ten of his own, driven into the centre of Karna's chest. The fight left nothing unhurt: the limbs of the two heroes, of their charioteers, of their horses, were mangled, and the blood ran like a river whose water no one would drink.

Arjuna rubbed his two arms and the string of Gandiva, and then the arrows came in floods. He sped cloth-yard shafts, nalikas, arrows headed like a boar's ear, razors, anjalikas, crescent-headed arrows — and they filled the sky like birds coming home to roost in the evening. Every one of them, every successive shower, Karna cut off with his own arrows.

Both armies, and the beings gathered in the welkin, were struck with fear at the sight of that wonderful encounter; and some among the spectators, filled with joy, raised their arms and uttered leonine shouts, waving their fingers and the cloths they held, whenever Arjuna rushed against the son of Adhiratha.

The duel went on until the sun itself seemed to disappear. Arjuna, furious now, drew Gandiva and loosed a weapon of fire — a blazing thing that covered the earth, the welkin, and the ten points of the compass, that hid the very course of the sun and set his own body alight with its glow. The robes of the watching warriors caught fire and they fled, and the sky roared like a bamboo forest burning.

Karna did not flinch. He answered with the weapon of the waters, the varunastra, and great clouds, dark as mountains, gathered on every side and flooded the field. The conflagration, fierce as it was, was quenched in a trice.

The two looked at each other across the wreckage of their arrows, and the armies of both sides shouted — the Somakas urging Arjuna to pierce Karna and cut off his head, the Kauravas urging Karna to slay Arjuna and send the sons of Pritha back to the woods forever.

It was Krishna who broke the silence. He had watched every exchange from the driver's seat of the chariot, and now his patience ran out. "What is this, O diadem-decked Arjuna," he said, "that Karna should succeed in crushing your weapons today?"

The calm of the charioteer had become the wrath of a friend who had watched enough. Krishna held out his hand, and in it turned the Sudarsana — the discus, its edge keen as a razor, the weapon that had felled demons and kings. "Putting forth your might," he said, "strike off the head of this foe of yours with this Sudarsana that I give you — as Indra struck off the head of his foe Namuci with the thunderbolt."

The discus blazed in the air between them, offered like an answer to a question no one had dared to ask. Through every battle of the war, Krishna had held nothing but the reins; now he offered his own weapon, and the duel hung, waiting.
reflection: Krishna, who came to the war holding nothing but reins, offers his own discus at the moment Arjuna's weapons fail — the wrath of a friend who has watched enough. The offer measures what the war has cost even the one who never lifted a weapon in it.
content_note: Fierce single combat with showers of arrows and a blazing weapon; blood is mentioned without graphic detail.
next_story_tease: But the duel was not to be settled by the discus, and the earth itself would soon swallow the chariot's wheels.
hero_scene: Krishna stands in the chariot holding out the blazing Sudarsana discus to Arjuna, whose exhausted bow-arm hangs low, while Karna's distant chariot waits amid the wreckage of arrows on the darkened field.
